annotations.description: Mulliganed a functional 7-card hand with 5 lands and 2 playable creatures (Black Cat on turn 2, Skullslither Worm on turn 4). While land-heavy, the hand has a reasonable curve and guaranteed mana. In Limited, this is generally a keep.
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. It has a functional curve (2-drop into 4-drop), correct mana, and will draw into spells. Going to 6 risks a worse hand for marginal upside.

annotations.description: Casting Hordeling Outburst before Bloodline Pretender misses a powerful synergy. If Bloodline Pretender had been cast this turn (choosing Goblin), then Hordeling Outburst next turn would trigger Pretender three times, putting three +1/+1 counters on it for a 5/5. By casting Outburst first, the three Goblin tokens are already on the battlefield when Pretender enters, so no counters are gained.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Hordeling Outburst on turn 3 mana, creating three 1/1 Goblins but missing the Bloodline Pretender synergy.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island from hand, then cast Bloodline Pretender choosing 'Goblin' as the creature type. Next turn, cast Hordeling Outburst to trigger Pretender three times, creating a 5/5 alongside three 1/1 tokens.

annotations.description: Casting Plaguecrafter with no creatures on board forces Gem31P to discard a card while only killing a 1/1 Goblin token - a very poor exchange. Taranika, Akroan Veteran was castable (it appears in the choices list) and would put a 3/3 vigilance threat on the board that could dominate combat against the three 1/1 tokens.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Plaguecrafter with no creatures on board, forcing a card discard to kill a 1/1 token.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Taranika, Akroan Veteran - a 3/3 vigilance that walls all three Goblin tokens and has a powerful attack trigger for future turns.

annotations.description: Casting Rummaging Goblin (1/1) over Bloodline Pretender (2/2 with growth potential) at the same mana cost. Bloodline Pretender choosing Goblin would be a better body immediately and would grow when Rummaging Goblin is cast next turn. The player has been mana-light (4 lands on turn 9), so Rummaging Goblin's filtering has value, but the board presence difference is notable.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Bloodline Pretender (3) choosing Goblin type - a 2/2 that grows with subsequent Goblin entries, providing better board presence while still leaving mana to cast Rummaging Goblin next turn for the +1/+1 counter trigger

annotations.description: Casting Burn Bright for 6 extra damage instead of using Flame Lash to kill Taranika while the opponent is completely tapped out. Taranika is an extremely powerful threat that makes another creature 4/4 indestructible each attack, and the opponent having 6 cards in hand means they could have protection spells available on future turns when they have mana up.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Burn Bright during combat for 9 total damage (opponent to 9 life)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Flame Lash targeting Taranika, Akroan Veteran while opponent is tapped out with no mana to protect it. Deal 3 damage in combat (opponent to 15) but remove the most dangerous threat on board. Burn Bright could still be used on a future turn for a lethal push.

annotations.description: Casting Chilling Trap in response to Taranika's trigger accomplishes very little. If targeting Angelic Protector (which has summoning sickness), the -4/-0 is completely wasted since it can't attack or block this turn. If targeting Taranika, it prevents only 3 damage while at 20 life, spending a card for minimal value. No Wizard is controlled so no card draw.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Chilling Trap in response to Taranika's attack trigger
annotations.betterLine: Save Chilling Trap for a more impactful moment — such as when the opponent has a lethal attack or to enable an alpha strike later. At 20 life, taking 3 from Taranika is fine.
